text:
Sounds like either round ligament pain or symphis pubic dysfunction (SPD). For some people a belly support band or physio can help. Some people just have to ride it out. 

For most people it mostly if not entirely goes away as soon as you give birth. It is worth noting that you tend to get it earlier in every subsequent pregnancy though.
I loved wearing clothes that showed off my belly. I thought crop tops were so cute. Even a cute Lil sweater over a bodysuit/romper was sooo cute. I could wear my belly band and no one could tell.

Honestly find yourself a good advocate who’s on the same page as you and understands your birth plan. Obviously if things change any medical professional will be able to give you a valid medical reason for it that’s not “you’re not progressing fast enough”.  

With my first baby, I was being seen by a midwife practice that was over seen by a hospital OB GYN practice. Before my midwife came to my room after check in the on call OB was telling me I wasn’t progressing and my baby’s heart rate was dropping. Mind you I came into the hospital transitioning from 7 to 8cm and the only reason they couldn’t establish my baby’s heart rate is the belly bands kept coming off because I was moving around a lot to ease contractions. I had my mom with me to advocate for me to have my natural birth. 

My mom kept asking “would insurance bill this as an emergency or elective?” Because if it is a true emergency they’d be able to easily justify the need for me to have one. Same with the episiotomy, the on call OB kept saying it’ll be “faster”. My mom said let her tear it’ll be an easier heal for my body to tear than to be cut. 

So if you can’t switch practices find an advocate to help you during labor. A partner, a parent, a good friend, a sibling or even a doula. Also make sure your provider has a copy of your birth plan so that they’re aware of what’s important to you and what your expectations are as long as everything goes smoothly.

text:

title: Zoe Journey & Other Compact Double Strollers?
text:
I know people asked about this stroller at least 2x but with limited responses.

Now that it has been in the market for a while, does anyone have a good/bad experience to share and/or recommend other non-SUV double strollers (ie not the Vista).

Our setup: we live in a highly walkable city with a lot of narrow spaces/steps. We used to have an Uppababy Cruz with our first baby which I grew to dislike after we got the Zoe Tour as a travel stroller but it quickly became our only stroller from 1 y/o. I have a STRONG preference for the most light/compact stroller possible and we have no habit of loading up the storage basket with a bunch of stuff. Many places we go to ask to fold the stroller so everything is usually in a backpack anyway.

We are expecting our 2nd kid when the 1st will be 2.5 y/o. I think she will be interested in the rider board soon but I am worried that we would still need a double stroller for some situations.

I am looking at the Journey because (1) it seems to be the lightest/most compact option and (2) we love our current Zoe.  
Concerns: (1) Double configuration has no storage basket at all - is that realistic with 2 kids?! (2) cost is not much lower than an UppaBaby vs quality is likely materially lower (I don’t want to buy a used Vista at price points available in my area, also I just really don’t like the huge size), (3) I don’t see a lot of reviews or local moms using that stroller and (4) we have an UppaBaby Aria infant seat that Zoe does not have an adapter for but this is less of a concern because we only used that seat on a stroller 2-3 times before the 1st baby grew out of it.

I am also open to hearing about other compact options I have not considered. I looked at the Momcozy ChangeGo but it looks just as bulky as the Vista.

Thanks!

title: Anyone been able to jog up to their due date?
text:

I’ve set the goal of doing as many 5Ks as I can for as long as I can, and not worrying about pace, which has helped stay within reasonable goals. I also think having a treadmill now (downhills outside are a little uncomfy) and actually using a belly band are helping. But it mostly seems to be just another way every pregnancy is so different. 

I’m taking it a week at a time, but curious if anyone has been able to continue running/jogging up to your due date? And any tips to do it safely/not destroy your pelvic floor? Should I be using anything other than a belly band?

title: There’s a light at the end of the tunnel.
text:
Aside from weeks 5-9 or so of my pregnancy, I worked my butt off (to keep my butt). I marched myself to the gym and continued to lift and run the entire way through. My last run was at 39 weeks and I had the baby 3 days later. Did I get hella slower and stagnate my weights? Did I wear a belly band? Yup. But did I still make it happen when nausea, fatigue, and insomnia were in the room? Yup. And I’m happy to report that I look like my pre-pregnancy self at 11 days postpartum. I’ve got about 15lbs to chip away at, but my old pants fit and the muscle definition is there. At the risk of sounding conceited I wanted to post this because 1. I’m really proud of it. I pushed through months of discomfort to try to set myself up for success. And 2. I know there are so many others in this sub with their heads down, grinding through some workout that feels lackluster, wondering if this is even worthwhile in the end. I think I can say it is. Keep hustling. You’re badass. 

Oh also I got him out in 4 pushes. God bless 🙏🏻

I had the exact same stats as you and carried low my whole pregnancy. Get into pelvic floor therapy asap, even if you think you have a good floor, and try to go to some gentle prenatal Pilates classes if you can. I had to avoid walking and hiking because it made everything so much worse. 

Also get a belly band (not the Momcozy one, a single band one that has compression) and if I were to do it again I’d get belly holding leggings. KT tape also helped.

I used a hip support cushion when I drove and sat on a ball at work. I also did a lot of pool time. 

Additionally, after you give birth, get a new referral for PFT and start going as soon as 3 weeks post partum. I’m very careful about baby wearing as well as it really makes things worse.

Good luck!   
\-An almost 6 month postpartum mama who carried low and heavy who still experiences significant pain and had to go on restricted Duty at work around 25 weeks.
